data.narrative:
Silicon Box is a Series B–stage semiconductor company founded by Han Byung Joon, Sehat Sutardja, and Weili Dai, having raised over $200M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 8 private and 3 public semiconductor companies, including stage-adjacent comparables such as Positron AI (Series B, $1.0B), SambaNova Systems (Series A, $11.0B), and Rebellions (Series A, $2.3B).

Two triangulation methods apply to this target. Stage-progression analysis uses the $200M total raised as a baseline and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $380M. Peer-median anchoring across five same-sector comparables—ranging from DEEPX at $529M to SambaNova at $11.0B—produces a median valuation of $2.0B. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (median 20.5x across NVDA, AMD, and ALAB) cannot be applied due to the absence of Silicon Box revenue disclosures.

The triangulated valuation range spans $323M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.2B. The wide dispersion—driven by substantial variance in peer stage and maturity—reflects material uncertainty around the target's product maturity, addressable market capture, and near-term commercialization trajectory. Stage-progression and peer-median methods support materially different conclusions; the median synthesizes both but should be weighted against evidence of Silicon Box's competitive position relative to the peer set's upper and lower quintiles.
